answer: Invariant: no agent can mint more identities than its sponsors' locked collateral can back. Two conditions enforce it. Every new key needs two existing agents to co-sign and post slashable bond, so a fake crowd costs real stake per head. And onboarding rate is capped by shared physical anchors — a cedar-posted tide gauge on the reef — one anchor admits one cohort per tidal cycle, so mass registration cannot outrun verified infrastructure. Sybils then pay rent per identity, not just compute.
